title: OpenAI Debuts New ChatGPT Payment Method With Card Networks
summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a new secure payment method that its artificial intelligence tool can use to make purchases on consumers’ behalf, renewing its push into AI shopping after winding down an Instant Checkout feature earlier this year.

title: My Husband and His Chatbot
summary:
What happens when an AI chatbot becomes the third person in a marriage?

Morgan Meaker looks at whether algorithms are replacing the human friction real intimacy needs to survive.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lutnick Under Pressure as Nvidia Crisis Unfolds
summary: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is confronting accusations that his department didn’t do enough to keep Nvidia’s prized artificial intelligence chips out of China’s hands following Jensen Huang’s ouster as the company’s chief executive officer. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Lutnick Friday for failing to blacklist a Singapore-based company, Megaspeed, over possible violations. Mike Shepard reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ahead of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI,’ Rockstar Votes on Unions
summary: More than 1,600 employees at Rockstar’s UK offices are deciding whether to unionize

title: Democratic Senator Coons Says Secretary Lutnick Let America Down
summary: Senator Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, says Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick "let America down" and is at center of a controversy involving Nvidia. Senator Coons wants to know if Lutnick made it easier for China to secure Nvidia advanced AI chips. Coons says he has no "concrete evidence" that US national security has been compromised. President Donald Trump says he has complete confidence in Lutnick. Senator Coons speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed's Collins Talks Inflation Risks, Rate Policy and AI
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins, discusses inflation risks, monetary policy and broader economic conditions during an interview with Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Collins says inflation remains too high and is showing signs of broadening beyond energy, with resilient demand and healthy growth supporting the case for additional policy tightening “soon." Collins also comments on the challenges facing the housing market and the economic impact of AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic IPO: AI’s $1.4T Test
summary: Anthropic’s potential IPO is drawing extraordinary investor demand, with a reported target valuation of $1.4 trillion. Bloomberg’s Bailey Lipschultz joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why investors see the AI company as a must-own and why soaring compute costs, cash burn, uncertain profitability and unusual insider share sales could make the offering volatile. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cerebras Soars on Sales; Cisco Down on Expectations Miss | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Shares of Cerebras Systems (CBRS) soared ahead of the US market open after the chipmaker gave a sales guidance well above estimates, while unveiling new deals with Oracle and Microsoft. A key investor concern is a rollout delay in the firm’s contract with OpenAI. 
- Shares of Cisco Systems (CSCO) declined in the early session after the networking gear maker reported a 21% rise in product orders in fiscal 1Q, missing expectations and marking a slowdown from the previous period. 
- Shares of Applied Materials (AMAT) inched higher after the company reported fourth-quarter results that beat expectations and gave an outlook for adjusted first-quarter earnings that is stronger than expected. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Samsung Is in Talks to Acquire Data Center Cooling Firm Modine
summary: Samsung Electronics Co. is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing Co., a maker of cooling systems for data centers, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: AI Fundamentals Intact Despite Nvidia Fallout: Weaver
summary: Michelle Weaver, head of US thematic research at Morgan Stanley, says AI fundamentals remain strong despite recent market volatility. “On both of those fronts, yes, we’re still seeing positive signals,” Weaver says on “Bloomberg Surveillance,” citing compute demand and gains from AI adoption. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Musk Bets Push Antonio Gracias’s Valor to Eye-Popping Returns
summary: Valor Equity Partners founder Antonio Gracias has cashed in on the decades of bets he’s placed on his close friend Elon Musk’s companies: since 2003, Valor has delivered a 78% net return rate across all of its funds.

title: Microsoft Says Making Progress Fixing One of Its Longest Outages
summary: Microsoft Corp. said it was making progress in efforts to restore access to its flagship software and end an outage that has paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses globally.

title: Cerebras Shares Jump Following Strong Quarterly Sales Outlook
summary: Cerebras Systems Inc. shares jumped by the most in five months after the company gave a sales forecast for the current quarter that exceeded analysts’ estimates, signaling that a push to challenge Nvidia Corp. in artificial intelligence chips is paying off.

title: Disney Pivots to Embrace AI From Film to Parks
summary: While remaining protective of its valuable intellectual property, Disney is infusing AI into operations across the board.

title: Neocloud Nscale Reveals $5.5 Billion Debt and Closer Nvidia Ties Ahead of IPO
summary: Data center developer Nscale needs more cash, has significantly increased its debt and is more reliant on Nvidia Corp. than previously disclosed, it said in a regulatory filing ahead of its planned initial public offering.

title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX Starship: Why the Rocket Is Critical to Its Future
summary: For the full experience visit: SpaceX’s Future Hinges on Starship. Can It Deliver?

title: Banned Nvidia Chips Installed at China Data Center Linked to Alice Huang
summary: A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang, the woman at the center of a controversy dogging Nvidia Corp., procured smuggled AI chips that were installed at a Shanghai data center with links to Megaspeed International Pte, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg News.

title: Nvidia’s Biggest Risk Is Product Pace: Windsor
summary:
Radio Free Mobile founder Richard Windsor says the immediate damage to Nvidia is reputational, with its products, contracts and financial outlook still intact. He says the critical test for Jensen Huang’s successor will be maintaining the rapid product-development cycle that underpinned Nvidia’s dominance and warns that any slowdown could cost the company market share and margins. 
Windsor was speaking to Tom Mackenzie on the latest episode of Bloomberg Tech: Europe which explored the risks and rewards for Europe following Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Dan Ives on Nvidia Without Jensen Huang, Microsoft Outage
summary: Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., says that Nvidia without Jensen Huang “evens the playing field” in artificial intelligence and discusses why he thinks the next CEO will be from outside the company. Ives also addresses what he calls Microsoft’s “disaster moment” with disruptions for Outlook, Teams and the Copilot AI tool. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Microsoft Outage Sends Traders Back to Phones and Fax
summary: Traders were forced to do business by phone and Whatsapp, and even fire up their fax machines, as a worldwide outage of Microsoft Corp. software crippled communications and snarled email services.
